subject: general
question: Girish Chandra Murmu held the post of ________ as on 31 March 2022.

options.text: Comptroller and Auditor General of India

solution:
The correct answer is __**Comptroller and Auditor General of India.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The current **Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG)** of India are **Girish Chandra Murmu.**
 
• The term **"Comptroller and Auditor General" (CAG)** refers to the **official auditor general of India**.
 
• The Indian Constitution's** Articles 148 to 151** **define this entity as an authority.**
 
• According to Article 148 of the Indian Constitution, the Comptroller and Auditor General of India is known as the country's top auditing body.
 
• They have the authority to examine all monies received and spent by the Indian and state governments, as well as any autonomous organisations and businesses that get significant government funding.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Solicitor General of India**

 
 
• ​The **Attorney General of India (AGI)** is superior to the **Solicitor General of India (SGI)**. They are the second-highest law enforcement official in the nation, and they work with Additional Solicitor Generals of India and the Attorney General. 
 
• In accordance with the Law Officers (Conditions of Service) Rules, 1972, the SGI and the Additional SGIs advise the Government and represent the Union of India in court.
 
 
 
• **Attorney General of India**
 
 
• ​The **Attorney General of India** serves as both the government's top lawyer and its principal judicial representative.
 
• **According to Article 76(1) of the Constitution**, they are chosen by the** Indian President **at the request of the Union Cabinet and serve at the President's leisure.
 
 
 
• **Chief Election Commissioner of India**
 
 
• ​The **Election Commission of India**, a body with constitutional authority to oversee free and fair elections for the President and Vice-President, as well as for state and national legislatures, is headed by the** Chief Election Commissioner of India**. **Article 324** of the Indian Constitution gives the Election Commission of India this authority.
